item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 132327
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Sun Sep 13 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Norbert, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, and on
newly formed Tropical Depression Fifteen-E, located several hundred
miles southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California
Peninsula.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&
Public advisories on Tropical Depression Fifteen-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ35 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP5.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Fifteen-E are issued
under WMO header WTPZ25 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP5.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.2N 135.3W
ABOUT 1655 MI...2665 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
ABOUT 1290 MI...2075 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 14 MPH...22 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was 
located near latitude 19.2 North, longitude 135.3 West. Norbert is 
moving toward the west-northwest near 14 mph (22 km/h), and is 
expected to maintain this general motion during the next couple of 
days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Some fluctuations remain possible, but a gradual weakening trend is 
forecast during the next couple of days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles (165 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Gibbs

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 18
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Sun Sep 13 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 140247
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number  18
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
500 PM HST Sun Sep 13 2026
 
Recent satellite imagery indicates that moderate vertical wind shear 
continues to displace any deep convection east of Norbert's center. 
Earlier ASCAT-A and ASCAT-B scatterometer passes depicted an 
asymmetric wind field, with peak winds near 40 kt north of the 
center. Given these data and Norbert's limited convection, the 
initial intensity is held at 40 kt. 
 
The initial motion is estimated to be 290/12 kt. The storm is 
expected to move west-northwestward to westward as it remains south 
of a low- to mid-level subtropical ridge. The track guidance 
continues to show good agreement on the general heading for this 
storm through the forecast period. The current NHC track forecast is 
largely unchanged from the previous advisory, and remains close to 
the corrected multi-model consensus (HCCA) and the Google DeepMind 
ensemble mean.
 
While some fluctuations in intensity remain possible in the next 12 
h or so, Norbert is forecast to begin a weakening trend that should 
persist through the forecast period. The cyclone continues to 
contend with moderate westerly to west-northwesterly vertical wind 
shear and SHIPS guidance is projecting the shear to gradually 
increase after 12-24 h. Simulated GFS and ECMWF satellite imagery 
show Norbert struggling to generate any deep convection by 48 h. 
Therefore, Norbert is expected to degenerate into a post-tropical 
remnant low around Tuesday, then dissipate by Wednesday. The current 
NHC intensity forecast remains in line with the corrected 
multi-model consensus (HCCA) guidance, which follows the previous 
advisory.

...DEPRESSION COULD BECOME A TROPICAL STORM LATER TONIGHT OR 
EARLY MONDAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM PDT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.0N 118.3W
ABOUT 680 MI...1095 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 260 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1006 MB...29.71 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression
Fifteen-E was located near latitude 17.0 North, longitude 118.3
West.  The depression is moving toward the west near 10 mph (17 
km/h).  A slightly faster westward to west-southwestward motion is 
forecast during the couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Some slight strengthening is expected overnight, and the 
depression is forecast to become a tropical storm by early Monday.

The estimated minimum central pressure is 1006 mb (29.71 inches).

----------------------
None
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------

$$

item.title: Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Sun Sep 13 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 140235
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP152026
800 PM PDT Sun Sep 13 2026

The depression has not become better organized since earlier today. 
Visible satellite images show that the well-defined low-level 
center remains displaced and exposed to the northwest of the main 
area of deep convection.  Using measurements with the Dvorak shear 
pattern, the intensity of the cyclone is estimated to be below 
tropical storm strength.  Thus the current intensity estimate 
remains 30 kt, which is in agreement with earlier scatterometer 
observations.

Water vapor imagery shows that the system is currently being 
affected by moderate vertical wind shear and relatively dry 
mid-tropospheric air.  Global model guidance indicates that these 
marginal to unfavorable conditions are likely to persist for the 
next few days. Therefore, only slight short-term strengthening is 
called for and the system is expected to begin weakening in a day 
or so, with the cyclone degenerating into a remnant low in 96 hours 
or sooner.  This is consistent with simulated satellite imagery 
depicted by the ECMWF model run.  

The depression is moving a little south of due west with an 
initial motion of around 260/9 kt.  A mid-level ridge to the north 
of the system should keep the cyclone on a mainly westward track 
with a slightly increase in forward speed for the next 72-96 hours. 
The official track forecast is similar to, but not quite as fast 
as, the latest Google DeepMind and corrected model consensus, 
HCCA, guidance.
